cim: Entrepreneur wins $50,000 at University of Arkansas at Little Rock artificial intelligence pitch competition - Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
cim_eredeti: Entrepreneur wins $50,000 at University of Arkansas at Little Rock artificial intelligence pitch competition - Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
szoveg_eredeti:
LITTLE ROCK -- A central Arkansas entrepreneur recently won $50,000 in technical development services at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock's second annual artificial intelligence pitch competition sponsored by Amazon Web Services.

Kelvin Bell, founder and CEO of Stratos Digital, took the top prize for his project, Victor AI, a bilingual AI agent that helps restaurants answer phone calls, take orders, answer menu questions and suggest additional purchases. The service is designed to understand a restaurant's menu well enough to accept phone orders and attempt one up-sell per order in hopes of increasing the business's profit margins, according to a UALR news release.

Bell said in the release that he has been interested in technology from a young age, adding the prize will be crucial to developing the platform.

"There's a need for this (service), because it solves the problems for an industry known to have high operating costs and low profit margins," Bell said. "I've been into technology since I was 7 years old, so this is the manifestation of a dream I've had my whole life."

Bell already has two restaurants in Arkansas using the service, which he said allows employees to focus on preparing food and other restaurant operations while leaving phone calls to the AI agent, the release states.

The competition's second year coincides with recent UALR efforts to expand its AI offerings, including the launch of a bachelor's degree in AI this fall, the first of its kind at a public university in Arkansas.

Other contestants included The Rockin' Chair founder Ashley Franke, who won $35,000 in services for earning second place in the competition. Her platform organizes accessibility information about live event venues in one place for customers with disabilities, according to the release.

Franke's service is already available through a website and mobile app. She said in the release she hopes to expand the platform through partnerships with event venues, which would fund the service so it remains free for fans.

In third place was On Paper, a service founded by James Hensley, who won $25,000 in technical development services. After being incarcerated, Hensley said he struggled to keep up with the various responsibilities and conditions required to comply with post-release supervision.

On Paper allows users to upload an image of their probation or parole conditions and provides reminders about their responsibilities and appointments so they can more easily comply with the requirements. Hensley said in the release the service helps translate legal language into simpler terms.

The app, which is already live, is aimed at helping people under probation or parole supervision avoid technical violations that could return them to incarceration, the release states. Hensley said approximately 70,000 Arkansans are currently under supervision.

"The different pitches showed that our Arkansas small businesses and entrepreneurs have highly creative ideas, and now the three winning companies will get some amazing support in accelerating their ideas with AI," said Laura Fine, state director for the Arkansas Small Business and Technology Development Center.

Tarek Anthony can be reached by email at tanthony@nwaonline.com.

Tarek Anthony is a higher education reporter and a recent graduate of the University of Oregon, where he earned degrees in journalism and political science. He previously served as editor-in-chief of the Daily Emerald and interned at Oregon Public Broadcasting and The Oregonian/OregonLive.
